Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Green Horizon Energy Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. Participants are reminded to mute their lines when not speaking to minimize background noise. As a reminder, this conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Green Horizon Energy's results for the third quarter of 2024. Joining me on today's call are Jordan Hale, Chief Executive Officer; Elena Vasquez, Chief Financial Officer; Marcus Lee, Chief Development Officer; Dr. Lena Kim, Chief Technology Officer; Sofia Grant, Chief Sustainability Officer; and Tyler Brooks, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call will contain forward-looking statements. We encourage you to review the disclaimer in our press release and on our website regarding these statements.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Jordan Hale.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Green Horizon Energy delivered exceptional results in the third quarter, showcasing our leadership in the renewable energy sector. Our success is attributable to our innovative technologies, strategic partnerships, and unwavering commitment to sustainability.

Today, I want to highlight seven key aspects of our performance. First, favorable PPA pricing trends and proactive contract extensions that have locked in attractive long-term revenue streams. Second, disciplined debt levels and declining financing costs that provide ample funding flexibility. Third, significant new PPAs secured at premium average prices, expanding our contracted backlog. Fourth, accelerated storage deployments and hybrid project advancements enabling firm dispatchable power. Fifth, robust gross and operating margin expansion driven by cost efficiencies and vertical integration. Sixth, strong construction progress across our pipeline with key commercial operation dates on track. And seventh, successful capital recycling through accretive asset sales, fueling new high-return developments.

These achievements position us strongly for continued growth in the global energy transition. Now, I'll hand over the call to Elena Vasquez to provide a detailed review of our financial results.

Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Jordan. Our financial performance in the third quarter was outstanding. Revenue reached $1.2 billion, representing a 45% increase compared to the same period last year. This growth was driven by significant project commissioning and increased energy production. Our gross margin expanded to 28.5%, reflecting improved operational efficiency and cost management. Operating expenses totaled $195 million, primarily due to investments in R&D and sales and marketing. Net income was $180 million, or $0.85 per share. We ended the quarter with $850 million in cash and cash equivalents. We are raising our full-year guidance for revenue and earnings.

Diving deeper into some of those key aspects Jordan mentioned, let's start with PPA pricing trends and our contract extension strategy, which form the bedrock of our long-term contracted backlog, providing visibility into 85% of our expected EBITDA through 2030. In a volatile market influenced by rising interest rates, supply chain normalization, and policy tailwinds like the IRA's PTC and ITC extensions alongside Europe's REPowerEU initiative, we've effectively secured strong pricing. Globally, utility-scale solar PPA prices stabilized in Q3 2024 at $26 to $32 per MWh on a levelized basis for fixed-price 15- to 20-year terms, up 8% year-over-year from $24 per MWh in Q3 2023. This reversal from sub-$20 per MWh lows in 2021-2022 stems from higher costs of capital with 10-year U.S. Treasury yields at 4.2%, requiring 7-9% unlevered project IRRs; ongoing module supply constraints despite TOPCon and HJT efficiencies reaching 23-25%; and merchant volatility in hubs like ERCOT and CAISO, where negative pricing has increased demand for fixed-price deals.

In the U.S., 60% of our 12 GW operating portfolio, Southwest solar PPAs with off-takers like APS and SRP averaged $28 per MWh in new contracts, a 12% premium over 2023, aided by storage mandates in California and Arizona. Wind held at $32-38 per MWh in the Plains via hybrid bids, akin to NextEra's Oklahoma deals. PJM pricing softened to $24 per MWh due to interconnection delays, but FERC Order 2023 reforms are helping. In Europe, post-energy crisis pricing is strong at €45-55 per MWh ($49-60 equivalent) for German and UK hybrids, up 15% YoY from TSO tenders and CfD auctions. Australia's uplift to AUD 55-65 per MWh benefited our 400 MW Queensland project under NEM reforms, while India's SECI auctions at ₹2.5-2.8 per kWh ($30-34 per MWh) offer solid returns with 25-year terms and VGF subsidies.

In Q3, we monetized 1.8 GW at a blended $30 per MWh—10% above market and flat to Q2—preserving full-year guidance of $29 per MWh on 4.2 GW signed YTD. Highlights include an 800 MW Texas solar-plus-4-hour BESS hybrid with a Fortune 100 tech off-taker at $35 per MWh, using our AI dispatch software for peak premiums, plus 20-year extensions on 40% at CPI plus 5%. Extensions added $450 million in NPV, with 1.2 GW of legacy assets—mostly 2018-2020 California and Midwest vintages—repowered and uplifted 12% to averages like $27 per MWh for our 300 MW Ivanpah-adjacent farm with PG&E, including curtailment credits similar to Enel's Sicily deals.

We're prioritizing hybridization with 70% of bids including 1-4 hour LFP storage for 20-30% firm capacity premiums, as in our ERCOT 500 MW pilot; merchant hedging hybrids like 70% fixed at $28 per MWh with collars; and 25% capex to high-price Europe and APAC for 10 GW in auctions. PPA pricing should hold at $28-34 per MWh through 2025, with upside from $22 per MWh LCOE on n-type TOPCon at $0.22 per Wp and EU Net-Zero Industry Act policies, mitigated by our hedged supply chain and in-house manufacturing.

On new PPAs secured, we added 1.2 GW in Q3, lifting our total contracted backlog to 4.8 GW, up 28% YoY for EBITDA accretion from 2025. U.S. highlights: 750 MW including 500 MW Arizona Desert Bloom solar-plus-200 MWh TC Energy BESS and 250 MW Mojave Wind with GE Vernova turbines to Microsoft and PG&E on 12-year CPI-escalated terms. Internationally, 450 MW: 300 MW Dutch North Sea Breeze offshore with Vestas V236 and Siemens hybridization to Equinor, plus 150 MW Spanish solar with LONGi bifacials to Iberdrola. Weighted average price hit $34 per MWh levelized, up 8% YoY, with U.S. Southwest hybrids at $37 per MWh (25-30% premium via storage and IRA $27 per MWh PTCs), Europe at $32 per MWh (offshore $48 per MWh), reflecting stabilization from NREL-noted lows, inflation pass-throughs, and hyperscaler demand. Backlog averages $36 per MWh, 65% fixed; we're targeting 800 MW-1 GW more in Q4 at $35-38 per MWh with hybrids.

Turning to debt levels and financing costs, gross debt stood at $5.2 billion as of September 30, up 8% YoY from $4.8 billion, funding $1.1 billion Q3 capex like $450 million non-recourse for 500 MW Desert Sun and €250 million for 300 MW NordWind. Net debt is $4.05 billion after $850 million cash and $300 million undrawn facilities, at 3.4x net debt-to-EBITDA (down from 3.9x YE2023), with FFO-to-net debt at 18% from 8.5 GW operations (85% PPA'd). Debt mix: 55% non-recourse project debt at 1.6x DSCRs; 35% corporate including $750 million 3.25% green bonds and $400 million term loan at SOFR +175 bps; 10% short-term bridges. Blended cost fell to 4.1%, down 20 bps QoQ/60 bps YoY via $300 million refinancing to SLBs at EURIBOR +140 bps (saving $12 million annually) with greenium, and $500 million green bonds at 110 bps over Treasuries. U.S. at 3.8% with IRA boosts, Europe 4.3%, APAC/LATAM offset by IFC. Maturities low at 15% next 24 months, $500 million swaps fix 70% floating at 3.9%; $2.5 billion facilities support 3 GW H1 2025 FIDs, targeting 3.0x delever by YE2025.

Gross margins hit 28.5%, up 320 bps YoY/150 bps QoQ, TTM 27.8% ahead of peers, from 42% polysilicon drop to $8.50/kg, BoM to $0.22/Wp, and 85% in-house U.S. cells (IRA 45X) yielding 24.8%. Americas at 32.1%, EMEA 26.8%. Q4 guide 29-30%. Operating margins 12.3%, up 250 bps YoY, TTM 11.9%, OpEx 16.2% of revenue via leverage; U.S. 15.2% from 45Y PTCs. Initiatives: $150 million supply diversification, AI inverters cutting BOS 8%, perovskite R&D for 30%+ efficiencies. FY25 13-15%.

Finally, capital recycling: Q3 sales of 1.4 GW generated $2.3 billion, like 850 MW Midwest wind to Brookfield at 11.2% IRR/7.8% yield (14.5x EBITDA). YTD $3.8 billion/2.2 GW redeployed to 1.2 GW Southwest hybrids ($45-50/MWh PPAs) and UK offshore. U.S. 75% volume, Europe strong; optimizes portfolio (fleet age 4.2 years, +2-3% P50), steady 3.8x leverage. $4-5 billion pipeline ahead.

I'll now turn the call over to Marcus Lee to discuss our project development activities.

Marcus Lee:
Thank you, Elena. Our project development pipeline continues to expand, with 15 GW of projects under development across various renewable energy technologies. We are making excellent progress on securing land rights, obtaining permits, and negotiating power purchase agreements. We expect to bring several new projects online in the coming quarters, further contributing to our revenue and profitability. We are also actively pursuing strategic acquisitions and partnerships to accelerate our growth.

On construction progress and CODs, our 4.5 GW pipeline has 1.8 GW under construction, 92% on schedule with EPCs like McCarthy and Bechtel at 25 MW/month. Solar (65%, 1.2 GW): Texas Horizon Solar (450 MWdc) 82% complete, first energy on 150 MWdc, COD Q1 2025; California Cascade Valley (300 MWdc) 68%, COD Q2 2025 with 100 MWh storage. Wind (400 MW): Iowa Prairie Winds East (300 MW) 75% turbines up, COD Q3 2025; South Dakota Buffalo Ridge II (100 MW) 95%, COD Q4 2024. Storage (200 MW/800 MWh): Arizona Ironwood 88%, COD Q1 2025; Nevada Emerald Peak hybrid COD Q3 2025. Southwest 45%, Midwest 30%, West 25%; hybrids 40% of FIDs, guiding 1.3 GW CODs FY25.

Dr. Lena Kim, can you update us on our technological advancements?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Thank you, Marcus. We are dedicated to driving innovation in the renewable energy sector. Our R&D efforts are focused on developing advanced technologies that enhance the efficiency, reliability, and affordability of renewable energy systems. We have made significant breakthroughs in areas such as advanced solar panel technologies, energy storage solutions, and smart grid technologies. On storage and hybrids: Q3 commissioned 450 MWh BESS (YTD 1.8 GWh, +65% YoY), efficiencies 92.5%, degradation 1.2%; ERCOT SunForge 200 MWh capturing $15 million ancillaries, CAISO Diablo Peak 150 MWh at $85/MWh LCOS, Australia 100 MWh. Backlog 4.2 GWh. Hybrids YTD 850 MWac to 2.3 GWac: Arizona Horizon 400 MWac at $42/MWh, ERCOT Lone Star 500 MWac +8% output. U.S. Southwest 60%, Europe/ Australia growing; de-risks intermittency, 28-32% EBITDA margins. FY24 guide 2.5 GWh storage/1.2 GWac hybrids, 10 GW pipeline.

We believe that these technologies will play a pivotal role in transforming the energy landscape.

Next, Sofia Grant will discuss our sustainability initiatives.

Sofia Grant:
Thank you, Dr. Kim. Sustainability is a core value at Green Horizon Energy, and we are committed to minimizing our environmental impact and contributing to a more sustainable future. We have established ambitious goals for reducing our carbon emissions, improving our energy efficiency, and promoting responsible resource management. We are also actively involved in community engagement and supporting local initiatives that advance sustainability.

Now, Tyler Brooks will provide operational highlights.

Tyler Brooks:
Thank you, Sofia. Our operational performance remains strong. We are focused on optimizing our operations, improving efficiency, and ensuring the reliability of our renewable energy assets. We are implementing best practices in areas such as asset management, maintenance, and supply chain management. We are also investing in training and development to ensure that our employees have the skills and knowledge they need to succeed.

I'll turn it back to Jordan Hale for closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you, Tyler. To summarize, Green Horizon Energy had an exceptional third quarter. We are confident that our strategic initiatives, our commitment to innovation, and our focus on sustainability will drive continued growth and success.

Operator, let's proceed with the Q&A session.

Operator:
Ladies and gentlemen, at this time we will begin the question-and-answer session. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
What are your plans for expanding your presence in international markets?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, John. International expansion is a key pillar for us, representing 25% of our capex allocation to capture higher PPA pricing in Europe and APAC. We're targeting 10 GW through auctions like Germany's EEG 2024 and Australia's LGC markets, building on successes like our 400 MW Queensland solar and Dutch North Sea offshore hybrids. In Europe, REPowerEU grants de-risk our 2 GW Baltic pipeline, while APAC/LATAM blended finance offsets spreads for 12% IRRs. We've secured offtake like Equinor and Iberdrola, with $1.2 billion tax equity enabling FIDs. This diversifies from U.S. exposure, aiming for 30% international revenue by 2026 without diluting returns.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with GreenCapital Partners. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins:
How are you addressing the challenge of intermittency associated with renewable energy sources?

Dr. Lena Kim:
Great question, Sarah. Intermittency is core to our innovation focus, addressed via storage and hybrids comprising 40% of new FIDs for 90%+ capacity factors. Our 2.3 GWac operational hybrids, like Arizona's 400 MWac with 200 MWh Tesla Megapacks, stack value for $42/MWh PPAs via AI controllers reducing clipping 15% and NREL forecasting. Fleet-wide, 1.8 GWh YTD BESS at 92.5% efficiency captures ancillaries, arbitrage, and firming premiums 20-30% above pure renewables. VPP aggregation and LCFS credits add revenue, with 4.2 GWh backlog at 14%+ IRRs. This scales renewables to grid parity, positioning for data center 24/7 demand.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Chen with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Mike Chen:
Can you discuss the impact of government subsidies and tax incentives on your profitability?

Elena Vasquez:
Absolutely, Mike. Subsidies and incentives like IRA's 45X/48E ITC/PTC are transformative, stacking to 50-70% with domestic content for sub-$25/MWh LCOEs. We've monetized $1.2 billion in transferability deals, boosting U.S. gross margins to 32.1% and project debt yields over 8%. 45Y/48E adders layer $27/MWh on hybrids, while SGIP and California's RA programs enhance LCOS to compete with gas peakers. Europe's REPowerEU and CfDs provide €45-50/MWh stability; globally, these underpin 28.5% gross/12.3% operating margins, with FY25 expansion to 13-15% assuming continuity. They de-risk 85% PPA backlog, enabling 15-20% growth.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Patel with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Lisa Patel:
What are your expectations for electricity demand growth in the coming years?

Jordan Hale:
Thanks, Lisa. We see robust demand growth at 3-4% CAGR through 2030, driven by electrification, data centers, and EVs—hyperscalers like Microsoft and Google committing 50 GW+ via REBA. U.S. Southwest irradiance and ERCOT/NEM peaks amplify this, with our hybrids capturing $10-15/MWh dispatch premiums. Policy like IRA and EU Net-Zero Industry Act accelerates, projecting 500 GW annual solar adds per WoodMac. Our 15 GW pipeline and recycling strategy position us to meet this, targeting 25% EBITDA CAGR to 25 GW operations by 2027.

Operator:
[Operator Instructions] There appear to be no further questions at this time. I will now turn the call back over to Jordan Hale for any closing remarks.

Jordan Hale:
Thank you all for your participation in today's call. We appreciate your continued support of Green Horizon Energy. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
